subject: Production: sudden latency & 5xx spikes after SDK bump - possible header/frame split
messages:
From: Sophie Patel <sophie.patel@meridianhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Production latency + 502s after SDK 2.4.1 upgrade

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in end-user latency this morning around 07:08 PDT followed by a spike in 502/504 errors. The only change on our side was rolling the Redwood client SDK from 2.3.9 -> 2.4.1 two hours prior.

Quick details:
- Impact: 8% of requests seeing 502s, median p99 latency up from 320ms -> 1.8s
- Repro: Happens against live inference route (route id: northstar-prod-v2)
- We've attached an excerpt of our logs and a short pcap around the incident window.

Sample log lines:
[2027-06-10T07:09:42Z] upstream_error: parser_error: unexpected header continuation
[2027-06-10T07:09:42Z] request_id=abcd1234 status=502 latency=1802ms

Can you confirm whether anything changed on the Redwood side or if 2.4.1 has a known regression? We are already fielding exec questions and need immediate remediation or a rollback plan.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Patel
Platform Ops, Meridian Health

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production latency + 502s after SDK 2.4.1 upgrade

On it — initial triage notes below. I pulled the meridian_error_sample.log and the pcap you attached.

Preliminary findings: 
- Multiple entries show parser errors indicating an unexpected header continuation token (see log snippet).
- PCAP shows HTTP/2 HEADERS frames where the :path header is split across consecutive CONTINUATION frames when proxied through Meridian's edge device. The runtime's streaming parser incorrectly treats the split as a malformed header and aborts the stream, which surfaces as 502.
- Error rate correlates with traffic that hits the proxy (approx 8% of requests), consistent with what Sophie reported.

Immediate ask from our side: Can Meridian confirm the exact proxy/fw version and whether any changes around header propagation were made in the last 24 hours? Also attaching a small binary pcap snippet for our infra team to reproduce.

Attachment: pcap_segment_0610.zip

I’m starting a focused loop with runtime eng to confirm whether the parser rejects CONTINUATION frames or mishandles header reassembly. Will update shortly.

-Dylan (oncall)

To: Sophie Patel <sophie.patel@meridianhealth.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: URGENT: Production latency + 502s after SDK 2.4.1 upgrade

Sophie — thanks for the quick report. We're treating this as high priority. Rishi is looped in for visibility at the exec level.

If this is related to the 2.4.1 client behavior we need to coordinate a rollback plan and an RCA timeline. Can you confirm whether Meridian can rollout a short-lived client rollback to 2.3.9 for a subset of traffic (canary ~10%) so we can measure delta? Marcus Lin

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sophie Patel <sophie.patel@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production latency + 502s after SDK 2.4.1 upgrade — root cause & mitigation

Summary of technical findings and short-term plan: 

Root cause: an interaction between Meridian's edge proxy and the updated client SDK changed header framing behavior. The Redwood streaming HTTP/2 parser in release 1.18.0 (runtime binary used by hosted routes) assumes header blocks for a single header field are delivered in contiguous HEADERS+CONTINUATION frames and validates certain header delimiting tokens. When the proxy splits a long header field across continuation frames in a non-canonical way, our parser deems it malformed and aborts the stream. The 2.4.1 client appears to produce slightly longer :path values for a common route which increases the likelihood of splitting.

Short-term mitigation (0-4 hours):
- We will push a compatibility guard in the runtime to coalesce CONTINUATION sequences more permissively and tolerate non-canonical splits. CI + canary rollout targeted to dedicated hosting nodes in us-west.
- Work with Meridian to perform a controlled client rollback on a 10% canary if they prefer faster mitigation on their side.

Longer-term (1-2 weeks):
- Harden the parser in a manner that strictly follows RFC7540 reassembly rules while validating edge cases across proxy variations.
- Add e2e tests covering header fragmentation cases and add to our perf/regression suite.

I’ll start the rollback-safe server patch now and provide timestamps for rollout.

-Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime Team

Attachments: triage_summary.pdf
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Patel <sophie.patel@meridianhealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: mitigation in place and next steps

Update for execs and Meridian team — short version: we deployed a server-side compatibility guard at 15:50 PDT to coalesce CONTINUATION frames more permissively. Early telemetry shows error rate back down to baseline and p99 latency returning toward normal.

Next steps:
- Redwood will run a full canary for 24 hours and push a fully hardened parser release in the 1-2 week window.
- Meridian: if you want to run a quick client rollback for confirmation we can coordinate a 10% canary during your afternoon maintenance window.
- Marcus/Rishi: please advise on credits/contractual remediation — Marcus to lead commercial follow-up.

Sophie, I’ll schedule a 30-min postmortem with your team and our runtime engineers tomorrow morning to review root cause, timeline, and prevention. Thank you for the quick logs and pcap — that made triage possible.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
